## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Niḷinikājātaka* (Ja 526) is a narrative in the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon. According to the opening framing narrative, the Buddha recounted this story while residing at Jetavana to address a monk who had been tempted and led astray by his former wife, reminding him that she had similarly caused him to lose his meditative absorptions in a past life.

In the story of the past, Indra is alarmed by the intense ascetic heat (*tapas*) generated by the ascetic Isisiṅga (Isisinga) and withholds rain for three years [Olson 2015]. Blaming the drought on the ascetic's spiritual practice, Indra instructs a king to send his royal daughter, Princess Niḷinikā, to seduce him [Olson 2015]. The princess succeeds in breaking the ascetic's chastity and destroying his mystic meditation [Olson 2015].
